text: Are immature men to blame for women not having babies? It's no secret that the birth rate in England and Wales has fallen to a record low. According to a new report, around 600,000 women will miss out on motherhood. So what could be causing this trend? According to a report recently published by the think tank Center for Social Justice, it could be due to a rise in immature men who are unmarriageable until much later in life. The report says that in the past, a 24-year-old man would have been likely to be married, have a child and been working for the best part of a decade. So this is the level of journalism The Times, the oldest national daily newspaper in the UK, has framing falling birth rates as a problem of immature men. Let's start with the source they're using. The report comes from the Center for Social Justice, published in March 2026, called Baby Bust, helping families realize their dreams of parenthood. This is not a neutral peer-reviewed academic study trying to objectively identify causes. It's a policy paper with a clear angle, pro-marriage, pro-family, pro-natal. Now, that doesn't automatically make it wrong, but presenting one think tank report as a primary explanation, without broader context, is at least a very limited way to approach a complex issue. But fine, let's take their own source. Even in that report, they include a poll data with a whole range of reasons why women delay or don't have children. 54% say motherhood is unappealing. 44% say child care is too expensive. 41% mention housing constraints and environments. 38% want to focus on their careers. 34% say they haven't found the right partner. So we have costs, housing, career timing, cultural attitude, environment, relationship formation, a complex multi-factor problem, and somehow the headline becomes immature men? Now, to be fair, in the video, presenter does briefly acknowledge that it's not just men. She mentions economic pressure, pension burdens, and structural issues that make starting a family harder for young people in general. And to be fair, the report itself does touch on the issue behind given framing. It talks about the pay and education gap for men and that the average age of living home for a young man now sits at 25. But notice what gets emphasized in the video, what gets reduced to a side note, and what is not mentioned at all. How about we stop just blaming men? And if men are falling behind economically, educationally, socially, how about we try to understand the reasons behind it? How about we stop portraying men and women as enemies and instead acknowledge that women have their challenges and men have theirs? And if we actually want to solve problems, including having more families and higher birth rates, we are not going to get there by blaming each other. We can only get there by working together.
